source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Fuel - Air Cleaners, p.6M-13

procedures.title: Polyurethane air cleaner element: clean
steps: Refit the cover and wing nut.

procedures.title: Oil wetted paper air cleaner element: replace
steps: Remove the wing nut, washer and cover.
Take out and discard the paper element.
Lift off the air cleaner bottom and discard the air horn gasket.
Clean the bottom and cover thoroughly (do not soak the bottom of a thermostatic air cleaner in solvent).
Check the bottom section seal for tears or cracks.
Put a new gasket on the air horn and set the bottom on the carburetor.
Fit the new element, either end up (both ends have the same plastisol seal).
Refit the cover, washer and wing nut.

procedures.title: Oil wetted paper air cleaner element: clean
steps: Remove the element.
Check the top and bottom seals; they must be smooth and even, with no distortion or cracks.
Hold the element up to a light bulb and look through it for punctures or splits.
Tap it on a smooth flat surface to shake dirt out without damaging it; compressed air may be used very gently, blowing against the normal flow direction.
Clean the inside of the cover and bottom; dry thoroughly if washed in solvent (never soak a thermostatic air cleaner bottom).
Reinstall the element.

procedures.title: Thermostatically controlled air cleaner: inspect and test
procedures.applies_to: all models (where thermostatic air cleaner fitted)
steps: Visual: check the heat pipe and hoses are connected properly and securely, and replace kinked or deteriorated hoses.
Operational: remove the cover and place a thermometer as close as possible to the sensor.
If the engine is warm, let it cool below 85°F; refit the cover without its wing nut.
Start and idle the engine; when the damper starts to open, lift the cover and read the temperature, which must be 85° to 115°F (a mirror helps if the snorkel position hides the damper).
If the damper does not open at the right temperature, go on to the vacuum motor and sensor checks.
With the engine off, the damper should be in the cold air delivery position.
notes: The system keeps carburetor inlet air at 100°F or more for better operation and warm-up; it has a temperature sensor, vacuum motor and damper in the air cleaner, vacuum hoses, an exhaust manifold heat stove and pipes (see figure 6A in the manual).
